incidents.vector: Active exploitation of three SharePoint flaws (CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, CVE-2026-56164) for remote code execution, IIS machine-key theft and persistence.
incidents.impact: CISA warns of ongoing compromise of all supported on-premises SharePoint versions; attackers are deploying malware and web shells and harvesting machine keys for persistent access.

incidents.victim: NATO/EU logistics routes and Ukrainian military
incidents.vector: Scanning for internet-exposed IP cameras with default credentials or outdated firmware, then using image-recognition software to analyze feeds of military transport and weapons shipments.
incidents.impact: Dutch AIVD/MIVD say Russia compromised cameras across the Netherlands, NATO/EU states and Ukraine to track weapons shipments; in Ukraine hacked feeds helped locate and target soldiers and equipment.

incidents.victim: Poland energy grid and European critical infrastructure
incidents.vector: Compromise of weakly protected routers and networking gear via default/weak credentials, SNMP abuse and old Cisco Smart Install flaws (CVE-2008-4128, CVE-2018-0171).
incidents.impact: EU/UK formally blamed the FSB for the December 2025 attack that nearly cut heat to 500,000 Poles; the UK/EU imposed first joint cyber sanctions on 24+ entities and 13 nations issued a joint advisory on ongoing critical-infrastructure router targeting.

incidents.vector: Attackers accessed a customer database held by one of Lidl's third-party IT service providers and exfiltrated part of its contents.
incidents.impact: Names, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth and customer numbers of online-shop customers in Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands were stolen; Lidl says no passwords or payment data were exposed.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion traced to an incident roughly three weeks earlier; data later published on the dark web by the Qilin ransomware group.
incidents.impact: Files allegedly taken from the central bank's network were leaked online; Libyan authorities are investigating the breach of the country's monetary authority.

incidents.vector: Abuse of trusted OAuth relationships via vishing-driven consent, compromised SaaS integrations (Salesloft Drift, Gainsight) and misconfigured guest access to query and exfiltrate CRM data.
incidents.impact: Microsoft detailed ShinyHunters-linked campaigns (2025-2026) exfiltrating Salesforce CRM records at scale across many tenants; a June 2026 intrusion at market-intelligence firm Klue (Storm-3138) reused stolen credentials against customer Salesforce instances.

incidents.victim: US municipalities, hospitals and financial firms (ransomware victims)
incidents.vector: First VPN Service (1VPNS) sold anonymity infrastructure and 'cryptors' used by ransomware gangs to hide their origin, disguise malware and manage exfiltrated data.
incidents.impact: US Treasury (with the UK) sanctioned 1VPNS and its Ukrainian administrator plus a Belarusian cryptor seller; the service, taken down by Europol/FBI in May, enabled attacks causing billions in losses to US critical infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service using edge-device exploitation, stolen credentials, a custom Go backdoor, an EDR-killer framework and a suspected zero-day; C and Go encryptors hit multiple OSes and ESXi.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 reports 'The Gentlemen' RaaS claimed 580 victims across 77 countries since 2025 (103 in manufacturing), with a 6x jump in the first half of 2026 and 117 victims in June alone.

incidents.victim: AdaptHealth, Nissan North America (Oracle PeopleSoft spree)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability in the Oracle PeopleSoft platform to access cloud-stored records and internal documents.
incidents.impact: AdaptHealth notified the SEC that patient data and internal documents were accessed; Nissan NA disclosed a related breach, both tied to a broader hacking spree against Oracle PeopleSoft deployments.

incidents.victim: Consumers with compromised home devices (NetNut/Popa botnet)
incidents.vector: Malicious SDKs bundled into smart TVs, streaming boxes and apps enrolled 2M+ home devices as residential-proxy exit nodes for the NetNut/Popa botnet.
incidents.impact: The FBI, Google and Lumen seized hundreds of domains and disabled infrastructure behind NetNut (operated by Israeli firm Alarum); GTIG saw 316 threat-actor clusters using its nodes to mask attacks in a single week of June.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion into the Japanese branch's systems resulting in theft of customer data.
incidents.impact: More than 4.38 million customers of Aflac's Japan branch were affected; the company had also disclosed a separate breach a year earlier.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion by the World Leaks data-extortion group, which exfiltrated documents after the company refused to pay.
incidents.impact: About 200,000 documents were leaked, including images of the unreleased iPhone 18 and its components (battery, chips, circuit boards) from the Apple supplier.

incidents.vector: Intrusion by newly launched ransomware operation 'Settra' against one of Taiwan's largest mobile operators.
incidents.impact: Pi Mobile was extorted by the group; the telco says its mobile-payments platform was unaffected, and Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs opened an investigation into possible data theft.

incidents.vector: The Cyber Anarchy Squad breached the company's network, wiping systems and deleting backups after stealing data.
incidents.impact: Hacktivists claim to have wiped 3,000 servers/workstations and 700 VMs, deleted all backups and stolen more than 650 TB of documents from one of Russia's largest construction companies.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion by a new group calling itself 'BLackField' that forced the company to take its entire IT network offline.
incidents.impact: The Japanese motor and electronics maker faces a $2 million ransom demand; it had also suffered a ransomware attack in late 2024.

incidents.victim: US National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)
incidents.vector: Network intrusion by the ShinyHunters group at the start of June.
incidents.impact: The US insurance sector's standards body suspended risk designations for insurers; some credit rating agencies paused data sharing to avoid exposure. NAIC says it evicted the attackers and is restoring operations.
